_comment: Mutation survivors accepted as a baseline for the core sweep. The nightly ratchet fails when a survivor appears outside this set, and when an entry is no longer a survivor. Regenerate with `python scripts/mutation_gate.py --baseline core --update` after a sweep, and only ever let this set shrink. Entries are the survivor line without its line:col position, so they survive unrelated code motion.

_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/decision.rs: de: Every branch dropped leaves the empty union, and `A ⊆ ∅` is the question the arm answers directly: whether `A` holds a value of its own. Deleting it hands the empty list to the union rule as a union of no branches, where the region reading refutes for a subject proved inhabited, proves for one proved empty, and declines for the rest -- the same three answers by the longer route. Checked over seven subjects across all three: an `int`, the bottom, a refinement whose bounds no value meets, a list of the empty element type, an instance, a `float` and a complement, which agree in every one. The arm is kept because it names the case the narrowing produces and answers it without building a union to ask about, and it is an equivalent mutant.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/decision/litera: A bare `Literal` is a table of one, and the arm says so on both sides of the pair. Nothing observable rests on it: as the subject the union rule places a constant its supertype lists by structural containment, and as the supertype the member fold refutes each member through the disjointness reading. Both answer the same and in the same number of steps -- the width-independence row reads one step either way, which is the whole query. The arm is kept because it states what the rule is about, and it is an equivalent mutant.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/decision/produc: Two fixed lengths that differ are refuted by the guard and, without it, by the position fold beside it: the shorter side runs out and the fold reports the mismatch. The guard was killable while that fold ended on the first answer that was not a proof; a fold that scans past a decline for a refutation reaches the same answer without it. The guard stays as the early exit -- it answers before any element is compared -- and is an equivalent mutant for the verdict.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/decision/record: Flipping the test that asks whether the order has already been read as unsorted sends the first lookup to the scan, which then never reaches the path that records the order -- so every later lookup scans too. Same shape as the row above: the cursor is never used and the scan answers, correctly and more slowly. The *other* `==` in the same function, the one the scan compares names with, is killed by `a_lookup_after_the_cursor_gives_up_finds_its_own_field`.

Reading every field list as unsorted puts the cursor on its scan for every lookup, which answers what the walk answers -- the scan is the fallback the cursor falls back *to*. It costs the walk and changes no verdict, so the permutation law over every spelling of a record passes either way. An equivalent mutant for the answers, and a slow one.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/descr/lines.rs:: The guard says *when* the pairs built so far are compacted, never whether the product refuses. The bound is `tidy`'s, and `tidy` is what the `?` beside this propagates: a union wider than [`MAX_LINES`] is wider whatever prefix of the pairs it is read over, and one no wider is built either way, so the two readings refuse on exactly the same products. Read as `<` the compaction runs on every pair rather than at the bound, which buys a copy per pair and changes no answer. What the guard is for is a working set that stays near the bound instead of growing to the product of the two counts, and the width of an intermediate is not a value any operation returns. `a_meet_is_bounded_by_the_width_of_its_union_and_not_by_its_pairs` drives the compaction in each of the four lattices; which pair it ran on is what no test can read.

_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/descr/regular.r: `BUILD_SIZE_LIMIT` is `8 * 1024 * 1024`, and reading the first `*` as `+` makes it `8 + 1024 * 1024` -- a megabyte where the constant says eight. It is headroom for the *builder*, and tightening it changes no answer the project gives: a pattern past it is `None`, which leaves the relation undecided and the walk untouched, since the walk runs the regex rather than the automaton. What it costs is completeness over patterns whose table sits between one and eight megabytes, and the smallest witness of that band is a two-thousand-state literal over sixty-two letters -- it builds in 13 s at eight megabytes and refuses in 85 ms at one. Thirteen seconds on every `cargo test`, and on every mutant of a shard already running fourteen minutes against a thirty-minute limit, is more than that line proves. So the band is left unwitnessed and the figure stays what its own doc comment calls it: generous headroom, with `MAX_STATES` as the bound that decides.

The arm joins the guards of two edges that reach one block, which makes a signature finer; deleting it falls through to the arm that reads the pair as the else edge, which makes every such signature coarser. A coarser signature can only merge more states, so the mutant is caught only by a language where the extra merge is wrong -- two states reaching one block by different letters. `merge_targets` runs first and leaves one edge per target, so the arm is reached only where a block holds two distinct but equivalent targets, and in that case both states are separated anyway by the blocks their other letters reach. Four witnesses were written for it, the sharpest reaching the block through separate equivalent targets after three letters, and wiring the component to descriptor letters did not reach it either. The arm stays because the refinement is what makes the partition the coarsest correct one rather than merely a correct one.

`rest_is_empty` asks whether the product's else edge is dead, and it is dead as soon as *one* side's guarded edges cover everything, because the pair takes the meet of the two rests. Reading it as `&&` keeps that edge and skips the canonicalisation under it, which spells the row differently -- and `merge_targets().minimal()` runs next and normalises the difference away. Checked rather than argued: a differential over 20,000 generated automaton pairs, comparing intersection, union and difference built both ways, found no pair the two disagree on. The line stays as it is because it is the cheap test -- one side's rest, already in hand -- and the mutant makes the machine build a state it then discards.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/ir.rs: replace: An empty shared clause list against a fresh empty one: the same value, and the same answers from every rule that reads it. What the shared list saves is the allocation a closed record would otherwise make for the empty list it carries, once per record built. A mutant that allocates instead is slower and identical, which is what an equivalent mutant is.
The empty field list, on the same argument as `no_clauses`.
The empty member list -- a sequence shape with no fixed prefix -- on the same argument.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-core/src/kind.rs: replac: `Kind::NoneType`'s region is `1 << 0`, and `1 >> 0` is the same value. A genuinely equivalent mutant, and the only one of the seven shift constants that is: the other six are killed by `every_kind_lands_in_the_partition_and_the_scalars_land_apart`, which requires each scalar kind's region to be non-empty and pairwise disjoint and every container kind to share the one that is left.
